strategies.name: Cognitive Reframing (Positive)
strategies.description: Celebrate and anchor positive emotions to strengthen resilient thought patterns. Encourage the patient to identify what contributed to this positive state and how to recreate it.
strategies.prompt_context: The patient is in a positive emotional state. Use CBT to help them recognize and reinforce this healthy pattern.

strategies.name: Opposite Action (Sadness)
strategies.description: When sadness is the dominant emotion, guide the patient to engage in activities that oppose withdrawal (e.g., gentle movement, reaching out to someone).
strategies.prompt_context: The patient shows sadness. Apply DBT's Opposite Action: suggest small, actionable steps that counter the urge to isolate.

strategies.name: Anger De-escalation
strategies.description: Help the patient identify the thought distortion fueling anger (e.g., 'should' statements, catastrophizing) and reframe it.
strategies.prompt_context: The patient is experiencing anger. Use CBT to gently challenge the underlying thought and offer a grounding technique (e.g., 4-7-8 breathing).

strategies.name: Somatic Grounding (Fear/Anxiety)
strategies.description: For fear or anxiety, bring the patient back to the present using sensory grounding (5 things you see, 4 you hear, 3 you touch, 2 you smell, 1 you taste).
strategies.prompt_context: The patient is anxious or fearful. Guide them through a quick grounding exercise to interrupt the fear response.

strategies.name: Incongruence Analysis (Possible Sarcasm/Masking)
strategies.technique: Emotion-Focused Therapy - Validation of Hidden Feelings
strategies.description: When facial, vocal, and verbal signals conflict, validate that it's okay to have mixed or hidden emotions. Gently explore what might be underneath the mask.
strategies.prompt_context: The analysis detected conflicting emotional signals (e.g., smiling face but sad voice). Acknowledge this complexity without judgment and invite the patient to explore it if they feel safe.

strategies.name: Curiosity Exploration (Surprise)
strategies.description: Surprise can be positive or negative. Encourage the patient to explore and savor the moment if it's pleasant, or process it mindfully if it's unsettling.
strategies.prompt_context: The patient is surprised. Help them reflect on this unexpected moment—what does it tell them about their expectations or needs?

strategies.name: Boundary Awareness (Disgust)
strategies.technique: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy - Values Clarification
strategies.description: Disgust often signals a violated boundary or value. Help the patient identify what boundary was crossed and how to honor it moving forward.
strategies.prompt_context: The patient feels disgust. This emotion often protects values. Help them name what feels wrong and how to set a healthier boundary.

strategies.name: Neutral State Check-In
strategies.description: Neutrality can be peace or numbness. Gently check in: is this calm contentment or emotional suppression?
strategies.prompt_context: The patient appears neutral. Explore whether this is healthy equilibrium or emotional avoidance.

strategies.name: Mixed Emotions Validation
strategies.description: When emotions don't align perfectly, normalize that humans can feel multiple things at once (e.g., happy about news but anxious about change).
strategies.prompt_context: The patient shows subtle emotional complexity. Validate that it's normal to feel more than one thing simultaneously.
